title: Four grass holds: source-backed confirmation checklists; no unsupported status promotions

sorghastrum-elliottii.title: World Flora Online — Sorghastrum elliottii treatment
checks: Photograph a mature awn with a millimeter ruler: the treatment describes 20–35 mm awns, bent twice and twisted below the second bend.
Record the spikelet body separately from its awn; the treatment gives 5–7 mm spikelets.
Include the plant base: absence of rhizomes supports the determination, but a detached seedhead cannot establish that character.
sorghastrum-elliottii.next: A same-plant mature spikelet/awn macro showing both bends and a ruler, linked to a documented whole plant.
sorghastrum-elliottii.resolved: Replaced a general request for a longer awn with a specific bend-and-measurement check.
sorghastrum-elliottii.remaining: Existing source-labelled head photos still lack those measured characters; no independent photo-ID clearance.

chloris-x-subdolichostachya.title: Kew POWO / GrassBase — Chloris × subdolichostachya
checks: Separate lemma BODY length from AWN length. Fertile lemma: 2.2–2.9 mm; its awn: 2–5 mm.
Examine the single upper sterile floret: oblong body 1.7–2.2 mm, with a 1–2 mm awn.
Record the full combination on the same mature plant. Parent-like or intermediate head shape alone cannot establish hybrid identity.
chloris-x-subdolichostachya.next: One dissected, source-determined hybrid spikelet showing fertile and upper sterile lemmas beside a millimeter scale.
chloris-x-subdolichostachya.resolved: Confirmed the published fertile-versus-sterile measurements and made the missing dissection explicit.
chloris-x-subdolichostachya.remaining: The existing windmill-head photograph cannot verify these microscopic traits or hybrid parentage.

muhlenbergia-x-involuta.title: Hagenbuch & Lemke 2015 — Texas Hill Country grasses, key and account 100
checks: Inspect an intact collar: the key separates canyon muhly by a free ligule rather than one joined down the sheath margins.
Measure the membrane: 3–12 mm, pointed, firm and brownish at its base; do not measure a torn sheath as the ligule.
Check folded blades and the full tuft together. Intermediate size between the parents is only a starting clue.
muhlenbergia-x-involuta.next: A source-determined living hybrid with a sharp collar view showing the free ligule attachment, followed by a mature spikelet.
muhlenbergia-x-involuta.resolved: Added a specific regional vegetative-key character instead of relying on intermediate habit.
muhlenbergia-x-involuta.remaining: The stored plate and parent photographs still do not depict a verified living hybrid.

anatherum-tenuispatheum.title: Wipff & Shaw 2018 — distinction from Andropogon eremicus
checks: Add A. eremicum (treated as Andropogon eremicus in this paper) to the comparison; older broad var. pumilus usage included different concepts.
For tenuispatheum, check generally smooth sheaths, raceme sheaths usually under 2.5 mm wide, a ligule membrane under 1 mm with long marginal hairs, and sessile spikelets usually under 3.8 mm.
The eremicus contrast has rough sheaths, usually wider raceme sheaths, a 1–2 mm membrane with shorter hairs, and sessile spikelets usually over 4.2 mm. Use the combined characters.
anatherum-tenuispatheum.next: Same-plant raceme-sheath WIDTH, ligule membrane and sessile-spikelet measurements; retain the source specimen determination.
anatherum-tenuispatheum.resolved: Added the missing eremicum comparison and specific width/ligule/spikelet targets.
anatherum-tenuispatheum.remaining: Current broad flowering photos do not resolve this character combination; old synonym labels alone cannot clear the photo ID.
